name: Schrödinger Spacetime
description: Anti-de Sitter space with one term added to its metric, which cuts its symmetries down to those of the free Schrödinger equation: Galilean boosts, a scaling under which time goes as the square of length, and a conserved mass. Dam Thanh Son, and Koushik Balasubramanian and John McGreevy, proposed it in 2008 as the gravitational dual of cold atoms at unitarity. Every event on a surface of constant time has the same future.
convention: The anti-de Sitter radius $L$ and the deformation $\beta$ are lengths. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$. We keep factors of $c$ explicit.
history: Cool a cloud of lithium atoms in a trap of light, and tune a magnetic field until any two of them scatter as strongly as quantum mechanics allows [ohara2002, son2008]. The gas that results, fermions at unitarity, has no length scale of its own, and its symmetries are those of the free Schrödinger equation, a group worked out in 1972 [hagen1972, niederer1972, son2008]. That group holds the Galilean boosts, a dilatation under which time scales as the square of length, $t \to \lambda^2 t$ and $x \to \lambda x$, one special conformal transformation, and the mass [son2008]. The conformal group of a relativistic field theory is the isometry group of anti-de Sitter space, and that match is one of the main pieces of evidence for the AdS/CFT correspondence [maldacena1998, son2008]. Can a spacetime carry the Schrödinger group the same way?¶Dam Thanh Son in Seattle posted an answer on 24 April 2008, and Koushik Balasubramanian and John McGreevy at MIT posted the same metric the next day [son2008, balasubramanian2008]. With a time $t$, a null coordinate $\xi$, the atoms' positions $\mathbf{x}$, and a depth $r$, $$ds^2 = \frac{L^2}{r^2}\left(-\frac{\beta^2}{r^2}c^2dt^2 - 2c\,dt\,d\xi + d\mathbf{x}^2 + dr^2\right).$$ Without its first term this is anti-de Sitter space in null coordinates, and Son's recipe was to add the one term that cuts its symmetries down to the Schrödinger group [son2008, herzog2008]. The mass of the Schrödinger group is momentum along $\xi$, so atoms moving in $d$ dimensions of space need a spacetime of $d + 3$ [son2008]. Balasubramanian and McGreevy called it "a strange aspect of the correspondence" that the geometry "has two extra noncompact dimensions" [balasubramanian2008].¶No vacuum has this metric: Einstein's equations ask for a negative cosmological constant and matter besides [son2008, balasubramanian2008]. Son supplied a toy model, a massive vector field pointing along $\xi$ [son2008]. Balasubramanian and McGreevy found the source to be pressureless dust, and built the dust from the ground state of an Abelian Higgs model, a superconductor filling the spacetime [balasubramanian2008]. On 7 and 8 July 2008 three groups, Christopher Herzog, Mukund Rangamani, and Simon Ross, then Juan Maldacena, Dario Martelli, and Yuji Tachikawa, then Allan Adams with Balasubramanian and McGreevy, each posted the metric with two dimensions of space as a solution of type IIB supergravity, and a black hole inside it to heat the atoms [herzog2008, maldacena2008, adams2008]. Two of the three groups got it from the geometry of a stack of D3 branes by the null Melvin twist, which Adams and his coauthors described as "a machine which eats supergravity solutions and produces new ones" [herzog2008, adams2008].¶Where does it sit among the known spacetimes? The bracket in the metric is a pp-wave, so Schrödinger spacetime is a pp-wave multiplied by anti-de Sitter's conformal factor, the form of Stephen Siklos's waves in anti-de Sitter space [balasubramanian2008, duval2009, siklos1985]. Siklos's waves need no matter, because their profile solves an equation of his, and $-\beta^2/r^2$ fails it [duval2009]. Setting $\beta = 0$ gives back anti-de Sitter space [herzog2008, blau2010]. Son pointed out that the term in $dt^2$ grows as $r^{-4}$ toward the boundary $r = 0$ while every scalar built from the curvature stays finite [son2008]. The spacetime is homogeneous, so each of those scalars is one constant everywhere [blau2009].¶How does a light cone look in a spacetime made for Galilean physics? Herzog, Rangamani, and Ross answered that its causal structure is "degenerate": every event on a surface of constant $t$ has the same future and the same past [herzog2008]. Veronika Hubeny, Rangamani, and Ross had proved as much in 2005 for a sister metric whose term in $dt^2$ goes as $r^{-6}$ [hubeny2005, blau2010]. One edge of every light cone lies in the surface of constant time, so a light ray can run along $\xi$ while $t$ stands still, and any two events at different times are joined by the path of a particle, as in Galilean relativity [blau2010]. Such a spacetime has no time function, no function that increases along the path of every particle and every light ray [blau2010]. Matthias Blau, Jelle Hartong, and Blaise Rollier called the structure "strongly Galilean" and "almost pathological" [blau2010].¶Son's coordinates come to an end: a falling particle reaches $r = \infty$ in a finite time by its own clock and meets no singularity there [blau2009]. Blau, Hartong, and Rollier continued them in 2009 with a new time $T$, $\omega t = \tan\omega T$, in which the metric gains one term, $-\omega^2(R^2 + X^2)\,dT^2$ inside the bracket, the potential of a harmonic oscillator [blau2009]. In these coordinates every geodesic runs on forever [blau2009]. The trap was already in the atoms' story: by a 2007 result of Yusuke Nishida and Son, each primary operator of their field theory matches an energy level of the same atoms in a harmonic trap [nishida2007, son2008]. The new time $T$ is the time of that trapped gas, so the same change of coordinates completes the spacetime and puts the atoms in the trap [blau2009].

related.text: The deformation switched off. At $\beta = 0$ the metric is anti-de Sitter space in its Poincaré patch, written in the null coordinates $ct$ and $\xi$ [herzog2008, blau2010].
The same line element with any profile $H$ where Schrödinger spacetime has $-\beta^2/r^2$. Siklos's waves are the profiles that need no matter, and this one needs some [duval2009].
Schrödinger spacetime is $L^2/r^2$ times a pp-wave of profile $-\beta^2/r^2$, and it has the pp-wave to thank for its light cones [balasubramanian2008, herzog2008].
The other spacetime of 2008 in which time scales as a power of space. It keeps time reversal and has no null direction, and so no Galilean boosts and no conserved mass [kachru2008, blau2009].

coordinates.name: Poincaré

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length; in four dimensions the cosmological constant is $\Lambda = -3/L^2$
Deformation length. At $\beta = 0$ the metric is anti-de Sitter space, and the boost $t \to \lambda t$, $\xi \to \xi/\lambda$ turns $\beta$ into $\lambda\beta$, so every $\beta > 0$ is one spacetime

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \xi, x, r)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\xi$, $x$, and $r$ lengths; $\xi$ is null, and Son's metric is $\beta^2 = 2$ at $L = 1$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \xi, x, \rho)$, the Poincaré chart's with $\rho = L^2/r$ for the depth, so that the boundary is at $\rho \to \infty$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Global

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length; in four dimensions the cosmological constant is $\Lambda = -3/L^2$
Deformation length. At $\beta = 0$ the metric is anti-de Sitter space, and the boost $t \to \lambda t$, $\xi \to \xi/\lambda$ turns $\beta$ into $\lambda\beta$, so every $\beta > 0$ is one spacetime
Frequency of the harmonic trap, positive. At $\omega = 0$ the chart is the Poincaré chart, and every $\omega > 0$ covers the whole spacetime

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(T, V, X, R)$, with $T$ carrying dimensions of time and $V$, $X$, and $R$ lengths: in the Poincaré chart $\omega t = \tan\omega T$, $r = R/\cos\omega T$, $x = X/\cos\omega T$, and $\xi = V + (\omega/2c)(R^2 + X^2)\tan\omega T$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cT$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{T}$ means $d(cT)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: General Dynamical Exponent

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length; in four dimensions the cosmological constant is $\Lambda = -3/L^2$
Deformation length, which the boost $t \to \lambda t$, $\xi \to \xi/\lambda$ rescales for every $z \neq 1$
Dynamical exponent, a pure number with $z \geq 1$: under a dilatation time scales as the power $z$ of length. $z = 2$ is Schrödinger spacetime and $z = 1$ anti-de Sitter space
The coefficient of $-c^2dt^2$ in the bracket, a pure number

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \xi, x, r)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\xi$, $x$, and $r$ lengths, and write $h = (\beta/r)^{2z - 2}$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
